g.text: Kafka Experiment: Producer and Consumer — Observed Interaction
No committed offset exists for kafka-experiment yet.
(Offset 0 was deleted by retention between sessions.)
Consumer is now idle. Current position (in memory) = 3.
No committed offset yet — autoCommit has not fired.
Same millisecond timestamp as the ProduceRequest.
Partition 0, offset 3, key and payload match exactly.
autoCommit (background timer, fires ~5s after handler returns)
CURRENT-OFFSET = 4 means "next fetch starts at offset 4".
Offset 3 is now the committed resume point.
On clean restart: resumes from 4, offset 3 not re-delivered.
On crash before this commit fires: offset 3 re-delivered on restart.
Crash recovery experiment (simulated with rpk group seek)
Simulates a crash before autoCommit fired.
LAG is now 3 (offsets 1, 2, 3 unconsumed by this group again).
The same event was processed twice with identical payload.
This is why TimescaleDB uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
and Redis checks timestamps before overwriting.
